segments.narration: These stairs climb straight into a ceiling and stop. Down the hall, a door opens onto a two-storey drop.
The house is in San Jose, California. Sarah Winchester, widow of the rifle fortune, designed it herself and kept crews working.
By her death in 1922 it held 160 rooms, two thousand doors and 47 separate staircases. So what was she building?
In 1906 the San Francisco earthquake wrecked large parts of it. She had the rubble cleared and simply left the rest.
That is where the stairs to nowhere came from. Not ghosts. Historians say she paused for months, and mostly managed her estate.
